_comment: MEASURED, NOT REASONED. Which Vitest/Playwright matchers does `undefined` SATISFY?
That is the whole question behind FUP-E2E-ABSENT-ROW-ASSERTIONS: `row?.field` on an
ABSENT row is `undefined`, so any matcher in `acceptsUndefined` turns a missing row
PROVENANCE: measured 2026-08-29 on vitest 4.1.11 by running every matcher against
`undefined` and recording which threw. Re-proved on every `npm run test` by
src/lib/matcher-vacuity-truth-table.test.ts, which reads THIS FILE and fails if the
runtime ever disagrees with it. Do not hand-edit either side: change the test, run it,
and let it tell you what the truth is.
WHY IT IS A FILE AND NOT A CONSTANT IN THE DETECTOR: the detector and the test must
share ONE definition, or the gate can drift away from the thing that proves it.
⛔ THE FUP'S OWN TABLE LISTED FOUR MATCHERS AND CONCLUDED `.not.toBeNull()` WAS `the
ONLY one`. It is one of TEN. The conclusion was sound for the four it tested and reads
as general -- the fifth wrong claim about this item, in the reassuring direction.

acceptsUndefined._comment: PASS when handed `undefined`. Split by what the assertion was TRYING to say -- the same matcher is fine for one intent and vacuous for the other.

theSecondFamily: ⭐ The FUP hunts assertions that a field HAS a value. The `claimsFieldIsErasedOrAbsent`
half above is the one it did not look for, and it is the WORSE half for Rule 12:
`expect(row?.purged_at).toBeFalsy()` on a row that was NEVER CREATED passes, and the
conclusion drawn is `the PHI was erased`. A fixture that failed to build its subject
⚠ `.toBeNull()` is SAFE (it throws on undefined) -- so the safe way to assert erasure
